question: At an arbitrary observed portfolio close, does a deep trailing one-year drawdown identify better subsequent entry dates than ordinary dates? Monthly income, amount, fixed-date DCA, a deadline to invest, and an investor's minimum holding period are not model inputs or preconditions. Separate buy-date quality from sell-date signals.
hypothesis: One fixed descriptive state: an unusually deep drawdown may precede a rebound, or may precede further loss. Its 0-100 historical depth percentile is not a validated buy score or probability. Do not invert the old score, try alternative windows, or select a horizon from these results.
priorExposure: Existing score and cash-timing studies used the same market history and examined drawdown states. This is a frozen historical replication for a different estimand, not untouched out-of-sample or formal control of the full search process.

market.calendar: Observed common product closes; multiply each provider-adjusted USD price by last FX on or before product date, no older than 7 calendar days. Expected 4206 dates, 2010-02-11..2026-10-30; compact JSON date-array SHA256 2e3851fc6cf968b09f2a1f33a76ff1eaa949e824537cdc9678a665333f65f952.
market.configuration: Fixed test portfolio USD (semiconductor ETF, not the currency) 30%, TQQQ 30%, zero-interest CNY cash 40%. It is not asserted to be the user's actual holdings or representative of other portfolios.

signal.reference: Start at 100. At each subsequent common close multiply by 1 + (.3*rUSD_CNY + .3*rTQQQ_CNY), in that arithmetic order. Daily constant-weight reference for the signal only.
signal.depth: After the t close, d_t=1-reference_t/max(reference[t-251:t inclusive]); unavailable before 252 closes.
signal.rank: Use all valid strictly earlier depths, at least 504. 100*(count strictly less + 0.5*count exactly equal)/N; unrounded double comparisons. No future observations or return labels. Flat history gives 50, not an artificial high or low.
signal.bands: high if score >=80, low if <=20, normal otherwise, on raw unrounded scores. Decision is after close, entry next observed common close. Include all eligible dates, not month-end or times of income. No historical or current score promoted to actionable UI while unconfirmed.

labels.primary: 12 months. 3 and 6 months are prespecified supporting descriptions, not independent replications or alternatives for selection. These are observation horizons, not instructions to hold.
labels.endpoint: Anchor at actual entry date, add calendar months and clamp day to target month length; take first common close on or after anniversary <=14 calendar days late. No unfinished, cross-phase, or invented outcomes. Signal, entry and liquidation must all lie in the same phase.
labels.account: One hypothetical unit, same amount for each date; .4 cash, buy .3 in each product including 10 bp buy fee, quantities .3/(1.001*entry price); hold actual units, no rebalancing; liquidate on endpoint with 10 bp sale fee. Market value between entry and endpoint includes cash. Max drawdown starts from wealth 1 before entry, includes buy cost, daily closes and actual terminal liquidation wealth (do not insert an extra pre-sale endpoint observation). Result in percentage points of unit, before personal tax. No deposit schedule or waiting action.

reporting: For each phase x horizon report n by band, mean/median/p10 net return, median/worst holding drawdown (nonpositive), high-normal and high-low median gaps and full Spearman midrank correlation. Quantiles linear interpolation at (n-1)*p. Report earliest day of each uninterrupted high run and its outcome, greedily counted nonoverlapping high windows (next entry strictly after last endpoint), and calendar-year concentration. Cluster indices are consecutive common signal dates, not calendar days. Counts are not independent trials.

decisionBeforeOutcomes.effect: At 12m separately in all three phases: high median exceeds normal median by >=1.0 pp, high mean > normal mean, high median > low median, Spearman >0. One pp is a project screening threshold, not a statistical discovery.
decisionBeforeOutcomes.risk: In each primary phase high p10 return and high median max drawdown must each be no worse than normal by more than 2 pp.
decisionBeforeOutcomes.coverage: In each primary phase at least 3 high runs across at least 2 distinct high-entry years, and >=3 nonoverlapping high 12m holding windows. Report high-run first-date results without treating adjacent runs as independent regimes.
decisionBeforeOutcomes.concentration: For each primary phase delete each represented entry year in turn, and each contiguous 12-calendar-month block entirely inside the eligible entry-month span. Remaining high-normal median return gap must be strictly positive; missing group fails.
decisionBeforeOutcomes.uncertainty: Primary later two phases separately: take all eligible dated observations together grouped by entry month (retain all bands), draw 12 consecutive calendar-month moving blocks with replacement until original month count, truncate last block; 2000 draws with Python random.Random(20261102) restarted for each phase. Require at least 24 represented month slots, at least 95% finite high-normal median gaps, and linearly interpolated 2.5th percentile strictly above 0. Report finite count and 2.5/97.5 interval when estimable. Descriptive due to dependent paths/prior exposure, not accuracy probability.
decisionBeforeOutcomes.groupPolicy: All primary gates conjunctive. Nonfinite/empty fails. Differences measured in percentage points; use 1e-10 pp for threshold equality noise, strict positive >1e-10 pp. No changing score, direction, threshold, interval or phase after seeing results. Do not replace a failure with positive pooled figures or a shorter horizon.
decisionBeforeOutcomes.integration: Only a historical screen passing all gates is eligible for further independent validation, exact production accounting / tax / data freshness and scope checks before release. A high depth percentile on its own must never appear as a confirmed buy score. No sell signal tested.
